report.summary: Chunk 4 of 4 of daedalus/mapping/inventory.py: defines check(), _by_key(), _statuses(), _describe_drift(), render_text(), main(), and module-level entry point. Includes gate mode, drift detection, and CLI argument parsing.
risks: check() docstring line 842-848 | medium | Claims four failure modes but code shows five (annotation_overreach). Check if annotation_overreach is defined elsewhere.
_describe_drift() docstring line 896 | low | Claims 'Every feature's DERIVED half' but function name is _describe_drift, not _by_key. Docstring may be misplaced.
main() line 941-943 | low | --refresh required but no default; if user passes no action, error message is 'nothing to do'. Might be confusing if user expects default behavior.
todos: Verify that annotation_overreach is defined and imported.
Check if _describe_drift docstring belongs to _by_key function.
Ensure main() handles all argument combinations correctly.

handoff.purpose: Provides check() for gate mode, drift detection helpers, render_text(), and main() entry point with CLI argument parsing.

symbols.name: check
symbols.note: Gate mode: validates inventory file, returns dict with ok, path, problems, stored, fresh.

symbols.name: _by_key
symbols.note: Returns derived half of features keyed by module or detector:reason.

symbols.name: _statuses
symbols.note: Returns dict of feature key to status string.

symbols.name: _describe_drift
symbols.note: Compares stored and fresh inventory, returns list of drift descriptions.

symbols.name: render_text
symbols.note: Returns a human-readable summary string of the inventory document.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: Entry point: parses CLI args and dispatches to check, refresh, or json output.

claims.text: Gate mode. Writes nothing; returns ``{"ok": bool, "problems": [...]}``.
claims.why: check() does not write anything; returns dict with 'ok' and 'problems' keys.

claims.text: Four ways to fail, in the order a reader needs them: 1. there is no inventory, or it cannot be parsed; 2. it was written by a different schema; 3. its digest does not cover its own derived fields -- somebody edited the mechanical half by hand; 4. regenerating it now would change something -- it is STALE, and the diff says exactly how.
claims.why: Code shows five failure modes: missing/parse error (1), schema mismatch (2), digest mismatch (3), annotation_overreach (additional), and drift (4). The docstring omits annotation_overreach.

claims.text: Every feature's DERIVED half, keyed by module (or by detector for the module-less stale entries). The human fields are dropped so a note cannot read as drift.
claims.why: This docstring belongs to _by_key function but is placed before _describe_drift. The function _by_key does implement this behavior.

claims.text: Field-level, not just status-level. A module whose importers or reaching entry point changed is a real difference, and reporting it as 'something differs, go diff the file yourself' is how a gate stops being read.
claims.why: The code in _describe_drift compares derived fields beyond status, including specific field changes.

claims.text: Mechanical fields are rewritten every run; human notes are carried forward and excluded from the digest.
claims.why: This claim is about the overall behavior of the module; the code in this chunk does not show the build function or digest logic.

claims.text: gate mode: exit non-zero if the file is missing, hand-edited or stale; writes nothing
claims.why: In main(), when --check is used, check() is called and if not ok, prints problems and returns 1; no file is written.

claims.text: print the generated document; writes nothing
claims.why: When --json is used, the document is printed via json.dumps and no file is written.

observations.what: Docstring for check() claims four failure modes but code implements five (including annotation_overreach).
Docstring at line 885 appears misplaced; it describes _by_key but is placed before _describe_drift.
main() requires --refresh for refresh action; if no action specified, it prints error and returns non-zero, which may be unexpected.
